title: WPPIL/36/2014 of Atma Ram Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION (PIL) NO. 36 OF 2014
Atma Ram .......Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. .............Respondents.
Mr. Ayush Negi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand / respondent no. 1.
Mr. Manish Kumar & Mr. S.S. Chauhan, Advocates for respondent no. 4.
Dated: 23.08.2014
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)
 This is a writ petition filed in public interest jurisdiction.
The prayers in the writ petition are as follows:
"(i) issue a writ or writs, order or orders or directions,
particularly a writ in the nature of certiorari quashing the
G.O. dated 14.3.2008 and all the consequential orders
thereto.
(ii) issue a writ, order or orders or directions,
particularly a writ in the nature of mandamus directing the
Respondent No. 1 to consider the representations of the
petitioner along with others.
(iii) issue a writ or writs, order or orders or directions,
particularly a writ in the nature of mandamus directing the
respondent No. 1 and 4 not to raise construction of the
proposed Municipal Solid waste processing and disposal
facility at village sheeshambara, derhadun."
2. Very briefly put, the case of the petitioner is as follows:
 Petitioner claims to be a social worker and a former
Pradhan. According to the petitioner, there are four places, which are
earmarked in the master-plan for the purpose of constructing the
landfill. It is while so, the impugned allotment of land has been made
in favour of the fourth respondent. It is his further case that, after the
advent of the Municipal Solid Wastes (Management and Handling)
Rules in the year 2000, the Rules have not been honoured. He would

2
point out that in the matter of selection of site, there are criteria. They
include:
"Site Selection
1. In areas falling under the jurisdiction of 'Development
Authorities', it shall be the responsibility of such
Development Authorities to identify the landfill sites and
hand over the sites to the concerned municipal authority for
development, operation and maintenance. Elsewhere, this
responsibility shall lie with the concerned municipal
authority.
2. Selection of landfill sites shall be based on
examination of environmental issues. The Department of
Urban Development of the State or the Union Territory
shall co-ordinate with the concerned organisations for
obtaining the necessary approvals and clearances.
3. The landfill site shall be planned and designed with
proper documentation of a phased construction plan as well
as a closure plan.
4. The landfill sites shall be selected to make use of
nearby wastes processing facility. Otherwise, wastes
processing facility shall be planned as an integral part of
the landfill site.
5. The existing landfill sites which continue to be used
for more than five years shall be improved in accordance of
the specifications given in this Schedule.
6. Biomedical wastes shall be disposed off in accordance
with the Bio-medical Wastes (Management and Handling)
Rules, 1998 and hazardous wastes shall be managed in
accordance with the Hazardous Wastes (Management and
Handling Rules, 1989), as amended from time to time.
7. The landfill site shall be large enough to last for 20-25
years.
8. The landfill site shall be away from habitation
clusters, forest areas, water bodies, monuments, National
Parks, Wetlands and places of important cultural, historical
or religious interest.
9. A buffer zone of no-development shall be maintained
around landfill site and shall be incorporated in the Town
Planning Department's land use plans.
10. Landfill site shall be away from airport including
airbase. Necessary approval for airport or airbase
authorities prior to the setting up of the landfill site shall be
obtained in cases where the site is to be located within 20
km of an airport or airbase.
Facilities at the Site
11. Landfill site shall be fenced or hedged and provided
with proper gate to monitor incoming vehicles or other
modes of transportation.
12. The landfill site shall be well protected to prevent
entry of unauthorised persons and stray animals.

3
13. Approach and other internal roads for free movement
of vehicles and other machinery shall exist at the landfill
site.
14. The landfill site shall have wastes inspection facility
to monitor wastes brought in for landfill, office facility for
record keeping and shelter for keeping equipment and
machinery including pollution monitoring equipments.
15. Provisions like weigh bridge to measure quantity of
waste brought at landfill site, fire protection equipments
and other facilities as may be required shall be provided.
16. Utilities such as drinking water (preferably bathing
facilities for workers) and lighting arrangements for easy
landfill operations when carried out in night hours shall be
provided.
17. Safety provisions including health inspections of
workers at landfill site shall be periodically made.
Specifications for land filling
18. Waste subjected to land filling shall be compacted in
thin layers using landfill compactors to achieve high
density of the wastes. In high rainfall areas where heavy
compactors can not be used alternative measures shall be
adopted.
19. Wastes shall be covered immediately or at the end of
each working day with minimum 10 cm of soil, inert debris
or construction material till such time waste processing
facilities for composting or recycling or energy recovery
are set up as per Schedule-I.
20. Prior to the commencement of monsoon season, an
intermediate cover of 40-65 cm thickness of soil shall be
placed on the landfill with proper compaction and grading
to prevent infiltration during monsoon. Proper drainage
berms shall be constructed to divert run-off away from the
active cell of the landfill.
21. After completion of landfill, a final cover shall be
designed to minimize infiltration and erosion. The final
cover shall meet the following specifications, namely:-
 a) The final cover shall have a barrier soil layer
 comprising of 60 cms of clay or amended soil with
 permeability coefficient less that 1x10-7 cm/sec.
 b) On top of the barrier soil layer there shall be a
 drainage layer of 15 cm.
 c) On top of the drainage layer there shall be a
 vegetative layer of 45 cm to support natural plant
 growth and to minimize erosion."
3. It is submitted that there is no buffer zone and there are
colleges and other Institutions, which are located in the close vicinity
and there is also reference to a religious place of great importance. He
would submit that while four places are earmarked in the master plan
for the construction of a landfill, it is illegal on the part of the

4
Government to have allotted another land. He would further point out
that the disputed places, where the land fill is going to be located, do
not find mention in the master plan.
4. Per contra, the stand of the fourth respondent is
essentially as follows. It is submitted by the counsel appearing on
behalf of the fourth respondent that the fourth respondent made an
Application on 03.01.2002 with the Mussoorie Dehradun
Development Authority (hereinafter referred to as 'MDDA')
requesting for making available land for processing and landfill site
for the municipal solid waste. By communication dated 27.02.2002,
MDDA informed that no land is available in the municipal limit and
requested the fourth respondent to approach the State to obtain the
land of the Gram Sabha through the District Magistrate. On
04.04.2002, the land measuring 4.047 hectares in Khasra No. 120,
Village Danda Lakhod was made available for trenching purposes. It
is the case of the fourth respondent that this is Site No. I. On
14.09.2006, the Ministry of Environment and Forest issued
Notification enforcing certain restrictions and prohibition on new
project making environmental clearance mandatory. Still further
more, he would point out that in the very same year, the Central
Government came with a Scheme JNNURM, under which 80 per cent
of the funds for setting up of the treatment plant was to be provided by
the Central Government and the remaining 20 per cent by the State
Government. Dehradun came to be selected one of such city under
JNNURM Scheme. On 14.03.2008, land measuring 8.323 hectares
was allotted for setting up a treatment plant as well as sanitary landfill
treatment with treated waste. It is this site, which is referred to as Site
No. II, which is in controversy in this writ petition. On 04.06.2010,
an NOC was given by the Airport Authority of India. On 11.07.2011,
the fourth respondent wrote to the Special Area Development
Authority (hereinafter referred to as 'SADA') to suitably change the
land use in the proposed master plan. It is submitted by the learned
counsel for the fourth respondent that the proposed master plan
includes this area for the purpose of landfill.

5
5. We notice further that the fourth respondent wrote to the
Secretary that the buffer zone as per prescribed standard will be
created at Site No. II. It is contended, inviting objections, the Expert
Appraisal Committee in its 119th meeting raised certain concern that
Site-II is in close proximity of river Asan. On such objections raised, a
joint inspection was conducted and, thereafter, NOC was accorded by
the Irrigation Department. The EAC at its 125th meeting
recommended for environmental clearance. While so, that Writ
Petition (PIL) No. 93 of 2013 came to be filed. On 24.07.2013, there
is a direction by this Court to the fourth respondent to remove the
solid waste from Site No. I to Site No. II. It is to be noted in this
context that the case of the fourth respondent is that in Site No. I
trenching was done. Site No. I has an area of 4.474 hectare and what
is proposed is to the removal of the entire waste to Site No. II. There
will be a treatment plant and, subsequently, the waste will be
landfilled. Site No. III, which is a little over an acre of land, will be
used as a place, to which the waste from Site No. I will be brought in
small vehicles and, later, carried to Site No. II.
6. On 16.08.2013, this Court observed that if the order
dated 24.07.2013 is not complied with, contempt proceeding will be
initiated. SLP No. 27363 of 2013 was filed in the Supreme Court,
which came to be finally disposed of by order dated 07.05.2014.
Since the order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is material, we deem it
appropriate to extract the same:
 "Leave granted.
 This appeal been preferred against the
judgment and order dated 16.08.2013 passed by the High
Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital in Writ Petition (PIL) NO.
93 of 2013 which reads as follows:
 "We are giving three more weeks' time to
comply with the order dated 24th July, 2013 passed by this
Court. In default, we shall be constrained to issue
contempt notice to the Chairman of the Nagar Nigam as
well as to the Executive Officer of the Nagar Nigam. On
the plea that the clearance has not yet received from the
Central Government, the Nagar Nigam is not discharging
its obligation of establishing a solid waste processing and
disposal facility. We are not bothered about establishment
of such facility, but we are bothered about removal of

6
those wastes from the vicinity of the people living in a city
which is claimed to be the capital of the State.

After we passed the order, the learned counsel
for the Nagar Nigam stated rearguing the case. We have
restrained ourselves from imposing exemplary cost on the
Nagar Nigam for that."
On 30.4.2014 this court directed the appellants to
file affidavit enclosing the supporting documents giving
the details of purpose for which trench has been made and
the timeframe by which it intends to complete the work.
 In their affidavit the appellants have taken specific
plea that the trench sites are meant for dumping the waste.
The following timeframe have been given:
"25. That in the above facts and background, the
Petitioners as is finding the situation impossible, is filing
this affidavit detailing out the status and time required in
completing and making the treatment plant operational
upon approval accorded by the MOEF, as under :-

A. (i). Site -I is currently operational, which is used
for trenching. This site the petitioner will continue to use
till such time proposed Site-II is made fully operational.
 (ii) One Site-II is made fully operational, Site-I
will be closed scientifically and will be developed as a park
as per MSW Rules, for which the Petitioners have already
got a plan approved and is in place.
(B (ii). Site-II all the requisite formalities such as project
report, DPR, financial clearance, construction plan, setting
up of treatment plant has already been obtained, the delay
is only because of MOEF clearance.
(ii) That on MOEF clearance being accorded, the total
time required to make the Site-II fully operational will be
approx. 18-24 months as maximum.
C (i). As aforesaid work at Site-III is almost 80%
complete and the balance 20% of the work, on stay being
vacated by the High Court, will take about 6-9 months
maximum.

26. That the total cost towards the project is approx.
24.60 crores, which has been duly approved and sanctioned
and the petitioners have been released two instalments and
the remaining funds have been duly sanctioned awaiting
release, which will help the petitioners to undertake the task
of completing the project at all the three sites, i.e. Site-I,
Site-II & Site-III, in the above timeframe. True copy of the
funds inflow and utilization by the Petitioners is annexed
herewith and marked as Annexure P-10 (Page No. 11-19)."

7
 They have enclosed the copy of the funds
certificate as also the report apart from the form of
utilization certificate.
 Having heard learned counsel for the parties,
we are of the opinion that the time frame given by
appellant Municipal Corporation is justified, as it will take
some time to make Site-II fully operational which may
take time up to two years. With regard to Site-I and Site-II
we feel that proper stand has been taken by the
corporation, who intend to fill up the current operational
trench at Site-I and after completion of the same and till
such time Site-II and Site-III will be made fully
operational.
 Sofar as MOEF clearance is concerned, we
direct the corporation to take steps for MOEF clearance at
the earliest, if not yet taken. The competent authority will
ensure that the clearance at an early date preferably within
a period of two months.
 In view of the stand taken by the Corporation
and the direction issued by this Court, we set aside the
impugned order dated 16.08.2013 passed by the High
Court of Uttarakhand.
 The appeal stands disposed of with the
aforesaid observation."
7. It is also the case of the fourth respondent that the Court
may consider that on 19.03.2014, the Court had directed the petitioner
to file a supplementary affidavit indicating an alternative land, which
may be considered for locating the disposal plant. The petitioner
sought time to file the affidavit on 22nd April, 2014. A supplementary
affidavit was filed in April, 2014, wherein the petitioner expressed his
inability to locate alternative land, but therein, reliance was placed on
the master plan, which shows that 11.50 hectares of land is reserved
for MSW.
8. It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the fourth
respondent that Him Giri University has approached the National
Green Tribunal and the National Green Tribunal was pleased to pass
the following order:
 "The prayer in this Application is for quashing the
Environmental Clearance apparently granted to Respondent
No.6 for setting up of a MSW Plant at Dehradun at the site in
question.

8
 It is now conceded before us that EC has not been
granted to Respondent No.6 as of now. However, the matter is
under consideration before the Competent Authority.
 Further it is brought to our notice that a matter in
relation to the site in question has been disposed of by the
Hon'ble Supreme Court of India vide its order dated 7th May,
2014 passed in SLP No. 27360 of 2013 preferred against the
judgment and order of the High Court of Uttarakhand in Writ
Petition No. 93 of 2013. IN view of the above, we are of the
considered view that it is not appropriate for this Tribunal to
examine the merit or otherwise of this case. Accordingly, this
Application stands disposed of partly it being pre-mature and
partly for the reasons afore-recorded.
 The Applicant would be at liberty to take such steps
which are permissible in law in the given circumstances.
 Accordingly, Original Application No. 76 of 2014 stands
disposed of without any order as to costs."
9. It is submitted that the petitioner has approached this
Court in the year 2014 against the allotment of the land made in the
year 2008 and he has been set up by the colleges.
10. As far as the challenge to the allotment of the land is
concerned, the allotment of the land took place in the year 2008. We
also notice that the Government of Uttarakhand has not filed counter
affidavit in this matter. No doubt, the petitioner has a case that the
petitioner was representing the matter. According to the fourth
respondent, in fact the petitioner has not filed any representation as
such. Even assuming that the petitioner has represented the matter,
we cannot overlook the fact that the petitioner has approached this
Court after a good six years. The question of delay or laches is a
matter to be decided in the facts of each case and more importantly
with reference to the developments, which take place in the
interregnum. We cannot completely ignore various developments,
which have taken place interregnum. Even more importantly, we
cannot ignore the fact that this Court had asked the petitioner to
indicate, whether any other alternative land is available. After taking
time, the petitioner has filed an affidavit, wherein he has expressed his
inability to locate any other alternative land. As far as the absence of
the location of the land in question in the master plan is concerned, the
case of the fourth respondent is that the land is located outside the

9
municipal limit for which the master plan has been prepared.
Therefore, this land can not possibly be shown in the master plan for
the municipal area and there is also a case for the fourth respondent
that pursuant to their request, the land will be shown in the master
plan, which is being prepared by SADA. As far as four places, which
were earmarked for the purpose of landfill in the master plan for the
municipal area are concerned, even as of today, the matter is not
entirely clear to us. Normally, we would have directed activities in
strict conformity with the master plan, but here also, we notice two
aspects. Firstly, when the fourth respondent approached the MDDA,
they were told that there is no land available. We asked Mr. Shobhit
Saharia, learned Standing Counsel for the MDD, though it is not made
a party, to get instructions. The instructions submitted are that in the
development plan, four locations are there, on which, this kind of
activity can be permitted and the area has to be acquired by the
Agency concerned and, thereafter, put to such use.
11. In this connection, we cannot also overlook the order of
the Hon'ble Supreme Court, which was passed in the litigation, which
was a public interest litigation in connection with the question. There
is also a case for the fourth respondent that it is a case where another
agency allotted a different land outside the municipal limits for this
purpose and therefore, it cannot be challenged by the petitioner.
12. We notice that in regard to the matter, environmental
clearance is yet to be obtained by the fourth respondent. We further
take into consideration, the order, which already has been passed by
the Hon'ble Apex Court. Still further more, we notice the stand of the
National Green Tribunal also.
13. In such circumstances, we would think that no relief can
be granted to the petitioner in this writ petition and, accordingly, the
writ petition is liable to be dismissed and is dismissed. Nonetheless,
we make it clear that this will be without prejudice to the rights
available to the petitioner, if the environmental clearance is granted.

10
14. We record the submission of the learned counsel for the
fourth respondent that apart from the construction of the compound
wall, no construction will be carried out except after obtaining
environmental clearance.
 (V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 23.08.2014 23.08.2014
Rathour
